title: Run multi-day wealth management work with agents
summary: Arca's lead AI engineer says agents do most background work at the wealth firm, tracking each client over tasks lasting up to ten days, while human advisors approve all money moves.
agent_role: Agents analyze client data, write code to build financial plans, track next steps and propose actions; human advisors make final decisions and handle all trades and money movement.
outcome: Arca's Aman Singh reports agents do most of the firm's background work, with tasks spanning up to ten days.
what_they_did: Arca built its own agent system for wealth management. It keeps a memory for every client: what happened, what is next, and who owns each action. Agents write code in a safe space to query client data and draft plans. Fixed rules stop agents from trading or moving money.
how_it_went: Singh says agents now guide the process, so "agents prompt people more than people prompt agents." A separate agent reviews advisor feedback and agent logs to suggest improvements.
worth_knowing: Safety limits are hard-coded rules, not instructions to the model, so risky actions like trades are never in the agent's hands.
prompt: Act as my personal finance assistant. Keep a running notes file for my finances: what has happened, what needs attention in the next few days, and what to track long term. Each week, review [my bank and investment statements folder], update the notes, and flag hidden fees, upcoming tax bills and deadlines. Propose actions with your reasoning, but never move money, trade or submit anything. Show me your proposals and wait for my approval.

curation.rationale: A real firm running agents on multi-day wealth management work with human approval gates; an interview with useful design details but few numbers and no reproducible setup. Finance boost applied.
